blocks.text: Where a book editor's hours actually go

Hard numbers on book editors are thin. The research turned up no large survey of book editors alone. The closest figures come from the Editorial Freelancers Association. Its rate survey, with 576 members, found freelance editors average 20 hours a week on billable editorial work. The same members spend about 6 hours a week on business tasks. Those tasks include invoicing, website work, social media and blogging.
That gap matters. Six hours a week is time you do not bill. It is also time away from the manuscript. That is the first place to look for hours back.

Office workers show the same pattern. Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index found the average employee spends 57% of their time communicating, through meetings, email and chat. The other 43% goes to creating, in documents, spreadsheets and presentations. That study covers office workers in general, not editors. Treat it as a pattern, not a measurement of your week.

Asana's Anatomy of Work Index 2021 gives that pattern a name. Knowledge workers, it says, spend almost two-thirds of their time on work about work. Asana defines this as communicating about work, searching for information, switching between apps, managing shifting priorities and chasing the status of work. Read that list against your last week. Most of it probably sounds familiar.

The job market adds pressure. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects employment of editors to fall 1 percent from 2025 to 2035. It counted about 105,000 editor jobs in 2025, with about 7,900 openings a year on average. The agency ties the decline mainly to print newspapers and magazines losing ground to other formats. Book publishing is not named in that explanation, so read the trend with care. Median pay for editors was $77,920 a year in May 2025. That figure covers editors in every field, not book editors alone.

Read the chart with care. The EFA figures come from freelance editors in 2020. They are not a time log of your week. Track your own day for one week before you decide what to hand off. Note which tasks take the longest, and which ones you dread.
What an AI assistant for book editors can do on your Mac

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. You hold Option and Command together to ask about anything on screen. It answers out loud. When you ask where something is, it draws a circle and a label around that control. When you ask how to do something, it guides you through the steps and waits for each click. Each of these has a job in an editing day.

items: Explain: ask what a sentence means, why a tense shifted or what a term refers to.
Point: ask where a menu, button or setting lives. Lazur circles it and labels it.
Guide: ask for the steps. Lazur walks you through them one click at a time.
Dictate: hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app.
Draft: ask for a query letter, a polite reminder or a note to an author. Lazur types the draft.
Research: start a background job that runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report.
Everyday: set a timer, add an Apple Reminder, open an app or link, or search the web by voice.

blocks.text: Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or an add-in for Word, Google Docs or Pages. It works beside those apps, on what is on your screen. That limit is the reason your file stays yours. You still decide every change.
Working through tracked changes in Word on Mac

Tracked changes are a common exchange in manuscript edits. In Word for Mac, the controls sit on the Review tab. Microsoft's Track Changes help page says you choose For Everyone or Just Mine when you track edits. Accept or Reject can act on one change, on all changes shown, or on all changes. Next and Previous move you between changes.

Microsoft's page does not list a Mac keyboard shortcut for Track Changes. Do not build a habit around a shortcut you have not checked. Ask Lazur to point at the control instead. It circles the button and labels it, so you can confirm you have the right one before you click.

blocks.title: Ask for the place, then the steps
blocks.text: Hold Option and Command and say: where is Track Changes in this Word file? Lazur points first. Then ask for the steps, and it waits while you click.

Here is a worked example. An author sends a chapter back with insertions, deletions and comments from two rounds. You want to accept the author's insertions and keep your own deletions. Ask Lazur to walk you through it. It names the menu, waits while you click, then names the next one. Check each change as you go. If a click lands wrong, undo it with ⌘Z and try again.
The common mistake is accepting all changes at once. That hides one bad edit inside a long run of good ones. Accept in small groups, and read each group before you move on.

blocks.title: Menu names shift
blocks.text: Menu labels can change between Word releases. If your Review tab looks different from the steps, ask Lazur to point at the control you need.
Google Docs and Pages for manuscript review

Many editors work in Google Docs. Suggestions there do the job that tracked changes do in Word. The two work differently, so read the suggestion panel before you accept anything. For the full browser workflow, read [Google Docs for book editors on Mac](/for/book-editors/google-docs). Ask Lazur to explain what a suggestion shows, and to point at the panel.

Pages works differently. Select the text, click Comment, then save. The steps are in [How to add a comment in Pages on Mac](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-pages). If you need a header or footer on a manuscript sample, see [How to add a header and footer in Pages on Mac](/how-to/add-a-header-and-footer-in-pages).
Dictation and drafting author queries

Queries pile up in an editing day. Hold fn to dictate a margin note at the cursor. Dictation returns clean, formatted text, so a note reads like a note. The personal dictionary helps with names that repeat across a book. A made-up town should not show up spelled three ways. Save a snippet for the standard line you send every author.

Then ask Lazur to draft the email to the author. Give it the facts first: the chapter, the change you need and the date. Read the draft aloud. Cut any line that sounds like a scolding. Send it yourself, from your own account. For more on dictation in long writing work, read [Dictation for writers on Mac](/for/writers).
Confidential manuscripts and your contract

An unpublished manuscript is often private. Your contract with the author or publisher may set rules for where pages go. An NDA may add more. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

Those are Lazur's stated terms. They do not replace your client's rules. Ask the publisher or your agency whether an AI tool may see pages. Do not assume a certification covers your case. Get the answer in writing if the contract is strict.

blocks.text: One question can fit two capabilities. Ask where a control is for a point. Ask how to finish the whole task for a guide. Ask what a sentence means for an explain. The wording tells Lazur which answer you need.
Mistakes editors make with an AI assistant
Most mistakes come from trusting an answer too fast. Watch for these.

items: Accepting a rewrite you did not read. Ask why it changed, then decide.
Letting a tool set the voice. The author's voice stays with the author.
Trusting a style rule without its source. Ask Lazur to research the rule, then open the cited page yourself.
Leaving a private file open in another window. Lazur sees what is on screen, so close what you do not need.

blocks.text: Check dictation output with care. Names, dates and figures are the usual errors. Read them against the source before they reach the file. A small slip in a name can cost you a reader's trust.

items: Download Lazur for Mac from the [download page](/download).

Hold Option and Command, then ask where the Track Changes or comment control is.

Track your own day for one week to see where the hours go.

faq.question: Is there an AI assistant for book editors on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold Option and Command to ask about what is on your screen. It answers out loud, points at controls and walks you through steps. It works in Word, Google Docs and Pages because it works in any app. It is not an add-in for any of them.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my manuscript for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It explains, points, guides, dictates and drafts. You make each edit in your own file, and you decide what stays.

faq.question: Is it safe to use an AI assistant with an unpublished manuscript?
faq.answer: Check your contract and any NDA first. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are Lazur's stated terms, and they do not replace what your client allows.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Track Changes in Word?
faq.answer: It can explain Track Changes and point at the controls on the Review tab. Ask it to walk you through accepting one change or all changes. Microsoft's Track Changes help page lists the options. Compare your Word screens with that page before you follow steps.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned but not available.

faq.question: Does Lazur listen all the time?
faq.answer: No. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Release the keys and it stops listening and looking.

faq.question: Can I dictate straight into my manuscript with Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots help with repeat lines and names that recur through a book.

faq.question: Can Lazur look up a publisher's style rule?
faq.answer: Yes. Research jobs run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, and they return a summary and a report. Open the cited pages yourself and confirm the rule before you apply it.

faq.question: Does Lazur replace a copyeditor?
faq.answer: No. It helps with lookups, reminders, drafts and the steps inside an app. Judgment on voice, structure and facts stays with you and with the author.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: Lazur has a Pro trial with no credit card. Check current plans and prices on the pricing page at /pricing before you commit. Plans differ in the number of AI actions they include.
